title: “Every dark pattern is a cost we've decided someone else pays”
summary: Campbell argues that calling a Ponzi scheme or a polluter profitable exposes a broken definition: moving a cost through time or space does not remove it. He traces Sol Price's ouster from FedMart, the Long-Term Stock Exchange, and Amazon's four-page Prime cancellation flow, and credits the book for the frame.
blockquote: A better definition of profit: leave people better off than you found them. If you don’t, you didn’t create profit. You destroyed value and moved the bill.
